chunks.content: ## Opening and Importing Files in CLO This section explains how to navigate folders and import garment assets into CLO, focusing on the use of the 2D and 3D windows. - Double-click the **British Files** folder and locate **Scene Details**. - Open the **Adding Smoking** folder. - Double-click **Dress Smoking** or drag it into either the 2D or 3D window to load the garment asset. - Use the fourth toolbar in the 2D or 3D toolbar area for further editing. ## Locking and Editing Outlines Covers how to use tools for locking outlines and selecting baselines to manipulate garment patterns. - Double-click to lock the outline line. - Use the **Loop Outline Tool** to select the baseline of the garment. - Use the **Rewind button** to loop the baseline to the inner line and drag the 2D line open to the inner line. - Lock the outline line using the Rewind button. - Additional locking actions involve interface panels and specific buttons related to garment details (exact names unclear but involve locking to inner lines). ## Using Tools for Pattern and Clip Adjustments Details tool usage for editing clips and dividing values, which impacts pattern manipulation and fabric simulation. - In the printer suite (likely a misinterpretation of a tool name), use the **etos drifters tool** (possibly a tool for adjusting drift or flow). - Use an icon resembling a fountain beside forecasting options to divide values by 50%. - Employ foundation objects designed for clips, which are crucial for accurate garment construction and simulation. - Use editor tools to select and adjust front and back panels on upper and lower sections. ## Simulation Settings and Fabric Details Instructions related to applying simulation settings, fabric properties, and improving 3D garment quality. - Turn on simulation and apply settings to the 3D costume to preview garment behavior. - In the object window, locate **Silk** and drag it into the object window to assign fabric properties. - Fabrics with good extension and weight (e.g., cowhide) create more detailed wrinkles. - Open simulation to confirm garment behavior in the 3D window. - Use the 3D toolbar to select the 3D tool, create fixed points on garment panels, and improve costume quality. - Confirm improvements and reapply simulation for updated garment behavior. - Use a 4-wheel tool in the 3D toolbar for further 3D clothing adjustments (exact function unspecified). --- This document captures the key procedures and tool usage for displaying smart folds and garment manipulation in CLO, emphasizing file handling, outline locking, pattern adjustments, fabric assignment, and 3D simulation settings.
